articles.title: Air India Express drops Hindon from its network
articles.summary: Air India Express is pulling out of Hindon Airport in the National Capital Region, barely a year after launching flights to Mumbai from there. This move significantly impacts regional air connectivity from Hindon, a civil enclave within a military airfield. The withdrawal highlights operational challenges at such mixed-use airports, potentially affecting domestic travel options for the NCR and surrounding areas.

articles.title: French sailor reveals flagship’s location via fitness app
articles.summary: A French sailor inadvertently revealed the real-time position of an aircraft carrier via his smartwatch while running. The vessel was sailing towards the Middle East, highlighting a significant operational security breach. This incident underscores critical vulnerabilities in military operations when personal technology is used, emphasizing the importance of stringent security protocols for all defence personnel.

articles.title: War in the Middle East: latest developments
articles.summary: In Beirut on March 22, a parking lot has become a makeshift camp for people displaced by Israel, where daily life continues amidst challenging circumstances. The scene captures a man doing his laundry, illustrating the ongoing humanitarian situation faced by displaced communities. This snapshot provides a glimpse into the broader regional developments in the Middle East, highlighting the human impact of displacement and the resilience of those affected.

articles.title: Denmark Learned in 1996 of the U.S. Iceworm Plan Under Greenland
articles.summary: Project Iceworm was a covert US Cold War initiative to construct a hidden missile base beneath Greenland's ice sheet. The remnants of this ambitious project, centered around Camp Century, reveal a significant historical effort to gain a strategic advantage. It exemplifies the clandestine defence strategies employed during that era, highlighting geopolitical tensions and innovative, albeit risky, military engineering.

articles.title: Three Turks, including serviceman, among dead in Qatar copter crash: ministry
articles.summary: A helicopter carrying three Turkish nationals, including a serviceman, and three Qatari servicemen crashed in Qatar's territorial waters, as confirmed by Qatar's defence ministry. This unfortunate incident involved personnel from both countries, underscoring joint military operations and the inherent risks in defence cooperation, even during training or routine missions.

articles.title: Submarine flaws minor, do not affect testing: Contractor
articles.summary: Taiwan's main contractor, CSBC Corp., has pledged to promptly resolve issues concerning the nation's first domestically built submarine. This move highlights ongoing efforts in Taiwan's critical initiative to bolster its naval defence capabilities through indigenous production, strengthening national security and self-reliance in military hardware.

articles.title: Supply chains face 'hard lockdown' amid escalating West Asia conflict: Kotak Mahindra's Anindya Banerjee
articles.summary: India is prioritizing crude oil, CNG, and LPG supply management amidst global supply chain disruptions from escalating West Asian conflict. This directly impacts national energy security and economic stability. India is implementing strategic measures to mitigate the challenges, ensuring resource availability and highlighting the critical need for resilient supply chains to counter international volatilities.
